subject: Dev tools renewal coordination sprint: GitHub / JetBrains / Atlassian
messages:

To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: JetBrains renewal options and alignment call

Hi Karthik,

Quick note — our account team ran the usage numbers and we have three paths for your 2027 renewal: standard renewal, team consolidation (discounts for bundling IDE + CLM), or a pilot for floating licenses across Dedicated clusters. I've attached a PDF with the latest quote (jetbrains_quote_v3.pdf).

If helpful, I can join a 30-min alignment call with you, Ben, and your procurement lead next week. Key questions we usually cover: seat count reconciliation, support SLA, and potential cross-product discounts if you consolidate with Atlassian seats.

Best,
Laura Kim
Account Executive, JetBrains

Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: JetBrains renewal options and alignment call

Thanks Laura — adding our internal owners.

Ben / Marissa — quick context: we have three separate renewal windows in Jan–Mar for GitHub, JetBrains, and Atlassian. Finance pushed for a coordinated review to reduce admin overhead and explore cross-vendor discounts. I put together a short matrix (attached) that reconciles current seats, avg active users, and our preferred procurement cadence.

Can you both review the attached renewal_impact_matrix_Q4.xlsx and flag any seat mismatches by EOD Tuesday? After that I’ll book a 30-min working session with all vendor reps.

Also tagging Vivek for any constraints on Dedicated capacity licensing we should surface to JetBrains if we pursue floating license pilots.

Thanks — Karthik
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: renewal_impact_matrix_Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet/xlsx, 54KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: JetBrains renewal options and alignment call

Karthik — reviewed the matrix. Two quick notes:

1) GitHub: our GitHub Enterprise seat count in the spreadsheet is off by ~120 seats; the active user extraction missed service accounts and a few infra bots. I exported the term snapshot from admin console and attached a plaintext snapshot (github_term_snapshot.txt).

2) Atlassian: Confluence growth is driving seat increases; we should push Atlassian for a usage-based cap rather than strict % overage fees.

If you want, I’ll draft a single vendor outreach that proposes a consolidated renewal timeline (one month window) and asks vendors for multi-product stacking discounts.

—Ben
Sr. Manager, Procurement Ops

Attachment: github_term_snapshot.txt (text/plain, 12KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: JetBrains Sales <sales@jetbrains.com>, GitHub Renewals <renewals@github.com>, Atlassian Account Exec <acct.exec@atlassian.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T14:29:00-08:00
Subject: Coordinated renewal request — pilot + pricing ask

Hi Laura / GitHub / Atlassian team —

Thanks for the initial materials. Redwood intends to consolidate our renewals into a single procurement sprint in February 2027 to simplify billing and reduce admin friction. Requests:

- Can each vendor provide an explicit multi-product discount if we sign GitHub + JetBrains + Atlassian within the same one-month window? Please state % or flat credit.
- For JetBrains: interested in the floating license pilot proposal (we run Dedicated clusters and would like license elasticity across pools). What telemetry / enforcement model do you require?
- For GitHub: we need a clear definition of seat types (human vs bot/service) for billing and a short-term bridge for the ~120 extra seats Ben flagged.
- For Atlassian: propose a usage-based cap for Confluence growth rather than fixed overage fees.

If you can share updated quotes or written commitments by next Wednesday (2026-11-10) that would keep us on track to finalize procurement paperwork in January.

Karthik / Ben / Vivek — after vendor replies, I’ll consolidate answers into a comparison sheet and route to Legal for redlines.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships Programs
Redwood Inference
From: JetBrains Sales <sales@jetbrains.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T16:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Coordinated renewal request — pilot + pricing ask

Marissa (and team),

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick responses below:

- Multi-product discount: JetBrains can offer a 12% stacking credit on top of standard volume discounts if we receive signed commitments for IDE seats and support bundles within the same 30-day window. We can formalize this as a credit line on the master agreement.
- Floating license pilot: We are open to a 90-day pilot. Tech requirements: a licensing proxy + periodic host attestations; we’ll provide a short integration guide and a small instrumentation SDK. Pilot is billable at a reduced rate; if successful, we’ll convert per the pilot terms.
- Seat reconciliation: we will accept a one-time bridge of up to 150 seats for Jan–Mar to account for service accounts with no extra fee; please provide a CSV export from your admin console.

I’ve attached an updated quote and a DocuSign placeholder for the pilot addendum reference (we’ll send the actual DocuSign link once internal legal approves).

Laura Kim
Account Executive, JetBrains

Attachment: jetbrains_quote_v3.pdf (updated)
